claims.head: Expect the Penguins to fire from everywhere
claims.call: The Penguins take at least their usual 60.2 shot attempts per 60 at 5-on-5.
claims.body: The Penguins shoot a lot, and the Capitals are near the bottom of the league at keeping shots down. Look for a big shot total.

claims.gist: The Penguins shoot a lot, and the Capitals give up plenty.

claims.head: The Penguins should get some good looks
claims.call: The Penguins’ average shot has at least their usual 6.7% chance of going in.
claims.body: The Penguins make their shots count, and the Capitals are around the middle of the league at preventing dangerous shots. Expect the Penguins to get some real chances.

claims.gist: The Penguins make their shots count, and the Capitals allow dangerous ones.

claims.head: Nobody’s sitting back in this one
claims.call: The game runs at more than 84.2 shots per 60 at 5-on-5, faster than either team’s usual.
claims.body: Pittsburgh plays some of the league’s fastest games, and so does Washington. We think this one runs hotter than either team’s usual.
claims.nums: Pace (shots per 60 at 5-on-5, both teams): Pittsburgh 6th (84.2), Washington 9th (83.3)
claims.gist: Both teams like a fast game.

claims.head: Airtight against leaky on the kill
claims.body: On the penalty kill, Pittsburgh is near the top of the league and Washington is near the bottom of the league. That’s about as far apart as two teams get.
claims.gist: The Penguins and the Capitals sit at opposite ends for penalty kill.
claims.call: The Penguins’ penalty kill allows less per 60 than the Capitals’.

WSH.head: Close, but Pittsburgh has the slight edge
WSH.body: Pittsburgh has had more of the chances over recent games and Washington has home ice. Washington’s best way to tip it is getting good looks.

PIT.head: Pittsburgh starts a half-step ahead
PIT.body: Pittsburgh has had more of the chances over recent games and Washington has home ice. Washington can still swing it if they get good looks.
